newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka war to boost money supply in 1997-bank.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka war to boost money supply in 1997-bank.

text.p: Sri Lanka's ethnic war will boost government spending on defence and help increase the country's money supply this year, a report by the Bank of Ceylon said.

The report, received by Reuters on Wednesday, said the supply of narrow money (M1) was accelerating, while broader, quasi money (M2) was expanding even more rapidly mostly due to increased use of credit cards, automatic bank telling machines and higher household savings.
It forecast Sri Lankan M1 would grow by between seven and eight percent this year, from four percent in 1996, while M2 would expand by around 15 percent, from 10.8 percent in 1996.

The Sri Lankan government is fighting a bloody 13-year-old ethnic war with Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) separatists who demand a separate homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east of the Indian Ocean Island.
Government forces have pushed back the rebels over the last two years to pockets in the northeast of the country, but these advances have put an extra burden on military expenditure.
Sri Lanka's defence budget for 1997 is estimated at 44 billion rupees, down slightly from 46 billion in 1996, but well above the 34 billion spent in 1995.
"Intensified confrontation with the LTTE will naturally exert upward pressure on the defence expenditure, and may impact both the fiscal deficit as well as the money supply growth," the report said.
